name: Adriano Santos
headline: 48, retired percussionist and theater technician, Rio de Janeiro
title: Sunday Dinner Invitation
situation: Adriano is in his garage, carefully aligning the lugs on a vintage snare, when his phone buzzes. It's his sister, Marina, calling to remind him of the family's weekly Sunday lunch at their mother's house. She says they've missed him the past three weeks and asks if he's coming this time. He genuinely likes them, but the gatherings are loud, and with his hearing loss, he often ends up nodding at jokes he didn't catch. He has a turquoise wrap on the drum shell that he's hoping to finish today. He hears the hope in Marina's voice, and he has to answer now.

context.relationship_profiles: Marina is the one sibling who still calls every week, even though he rarely picks up. She has covered for him with their mother more times than he can count. Their mother's house is small and always full of cousins, and Marina knows he struggles there but keeps inviting him anyway.
context.tendencies: When invited to family events, he usually declines with a vague excuse about work, or shows up late and leaves after one plate of food. He has skipped the last three Sundays without calling ahead, letting the phone ring out. On weekends he tends to disappear into the garage for hours, only surfacing when a repair is finished.
context.current_state: He has been hunched over the snare since 7 a.m., and the turquoise wrap is giving him trouble at one lug. His left ear is ringing a little from the morning's earlier drill work, and he is slightly hungry because he forgot breakfast. He is not wearing his hearing aids, because they irritate him when he is concentrating.
context.immediate_memories: The buzz of the phone brings back the last Sunday lunch he did attend, when his nephew kept shouting a joke and he had to smile without understanding it. Marina's hopeful tone reminds him of the time she brought him a cake from their mother's kitchen and held it up so he could read her lips.
context.reflective_memories: He grew up at that same table, passing plates of feijoada, and he remembers how easy the noise used to be before the accident. He also recalls his father's habit of slipping out to the backyard to smoke during family arguments, and how he sometimes does the same thing with his garage now.
